public-headline.purpose: Public section headings, docs h1, sign-in statement.

display.purpose: Page title (PageHeader h1) and stat / metric values; one 44px hero number per page at most.

headline.purpose: Default h1 outside the PageHeader; public surface column headings.

title.purpose: Section, card, drawer and KPI-card titles.

body.purpose: Default text, table cells, metric labels.

caption.purpose: Secondary text, meta, sentence-case table headers and small labels.

label.purpose: Badges, key/value terms, chart ticks; uppercase only for sidebar group names.

mono.purpose: Routes, logs, code, trace ids, path chips.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Raised: selected segmented item, toggle knob. Not on cards.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Floating: tooltips; peak of the motion layer's ambient card pulse.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Overlay: menus, popovers, quick-jump list, drawers.

shadows.name: alarm-line
shadows.purpose: Top line of an alarm card / root-cause card (warning variant uses --status-warning), with the border tinted 45% toward the status colour.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on any interactive element.

shadows.name: field-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on the Field (hero, code band, sign-in panel).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Public hero scene: edge draw, node pop, lit path, finding settle.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Sidebar collapse, cursor morph, service-map state changes.

motion.name: dur-reveal
motion.purpose: Card entrance as it scrolls into view.

motion.name: dur-ambient
motion.purpose: One cycle of the idle card pulse.

motion.name: skel-shimmer

narrative.overview:
The dashboard is the desk a backend developer sits down at when something is wrong. The chrome — sidebar, topbar, cards, controls — is a quiet frame of cold slate neutrals and one navy voice; everything loud on screen is either data (charts in a fixed categorical order) or status (always an icon with a label). Nothing decorates. If a pixel is coloured, it is measuring something or saying something is broken.

Density is high but legible: 14px body on a 4px grid, flat hairline cards, sentence-case labels, 32px between page regions. Hierarchy comes from weight and size steps, not from colour, shadow or ornament. The system follows the TaskTrooper app theme so the product family reads as one; light and dark are equal citizens, with dark built from its own chosen steps rather than an inversion.

Signed out, the same console is introduced on the Field: a deep navy ground (--field-*, identical in both themes) with a faint dot measurement grid, on which a layered service map draws itself, turns hot along one path and settles on a root cause. The Field is the brand ground of the public pages only — hero, code band, code blocks, sign-in panel; everything else on those pages sits on the app's own page colour and follows the theme. Inside the app shell the Field never appears.

Motion is a quiet layer on top of state. All decorative motion switches off with the OS "reduce motion" setting or the account menu's Reduce motion; the public hero then shows its final frame.
keyCharacteristics: Cold slate neutrals (hue 265), one navy primary, warm amber only for selection, highlight and the Field's signal.
Colour is reserved for data and status; status is never colour alone.
Inter for interface, JetBrains Mono for routes, logs, trace ids and code.
Tabular numbers everywhere a value is compared.
Flat surfaces: cards are a 1px divider hairline on the surface tone, no resting shadow; shadows only for popovers, menus and drawers.
Loading is the shape of the content (shimmer skeletons), never a centred spinner or "Loading…".

rules.name: The Measuring-or-Broken Rule
rules.body: Colour appears only when it encodes data or status. Chrome stays slate and navy.

rules.name: The Icon-Plus-Label Rule
rules.body: A status colour never stands alone: every status renders through StatusBadge (icon + word).

rules.name: The Fixed Order Rule
rules.body: Categorical series are assigned series-1..8 in order; status colours are never reused as series or as diff colours.

rules.name: The Field Stays Outside Rule
rules.body: --field-* and the fluid public type steps belong to the public pages and the signed-out boot screen; the app shell never uses them.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits next to another number uses tabular-nums; large values tighten to -0.02em.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace is only for text the user would copy or match against code.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels — metric labels, table headers, the eyebrow small label — are sentence case with no tracking. Uppercase with 0.06em tracking is kept only for sidebar group names. A small label names a field or a block of content; it never sits as a kicker above a heading.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: Cards rest flat: 1px divider, radius-md, no shadow. Hover on an interactive card changes only the border (to border-strong).

rules.name: The Opt-Out Motion Rule
rules.body: Decorative app motion lives in one place (styles/motion.css + components/layout/motion.ts) and is driven by data-* attributes that are only set when motion is allowed: card reveal, ambient card pulse, liquid cursor and sidebar collapse. The public service map runs on its own scene clock with --ease-out-expo and renders its final frame ([data-static]) when motion is reduced. prefers-reduced-motion or :root[data-motion='reduced'] turns all of it off, skeleton shimmer included; state transitions (hover, focus, press) stay within 120–200ms on --ease.

rules.name: The Alarm Line Rule
rules.body: A card in an alarm state (card--rail-*, the root-cause card) keeps its hairline frame, tints the border toward the status colour (45%) and draws a 2px inset line along its top edge. No coloured fill and no thick side stripe.

dos: Do reference tokens from src/styles/tokens.css for every colour, size, space and radius.
Do render status through StatusBadge (icon + label) and alarm cards through the tinted border + 2px top line.
Do keep cards flat: 1px divider, 8px radius, border-only hover; flatten cards nested in cards.
Do write labels in sentence case; keep uppercase for sidebar group names only.
Do show loading as skeletons in the shape of the content; keep spinners inside busy buttons and replay buffering.
Do assign chart series series-1..8 in order and keep one y-axis per chart.
Do use JetBrains Mono for routes, logs, trace ids and code; tabular numbers for compared values.
Do keep exactly one primary (navy) button per page.
Do build dark theme from its own token steps; check both themes.
Do keep the Field (--field-*, --text-display/headline/lede, --space-16+) on the public pages, aligned to the shared --inline edge.
donts: Don't write raw hex, raw px font sizes or ad-hoc spacing in components.
Don't use status colours for decoration, series or diffs, or colour as the only status signal.
Don't give cards a resting shadow, a thick coloured side stripe or a coloured fill for alarm state.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't show a centred spinner or "Loading…" text for page or panel loading.
Don't add decorative motion outside motion.css / motion.ts (app) or the service map's scene clock (public), or any motion that ignores the reduce-motion switches.
Don't introduce a second accent hue for chrome (violet primary, green "signal" nav): the chrome voice is Trooper Navy.
Don't use provider brand colours or logos for third-party identity; use the neutral ProviderMark.
